l.i: Impp, Diocletianus & Maximianus Augusti Papiniano.
Liberos à parentibus neque venditionis, neque donationis titulo, neque pignoris iure, aut
aliquo quolibet modo, nec sub prætextu ignorantiæ accipientis in alium transferri posse,
manifestissimi iuris est.

main_text.l: Cùm tamen obtineri non posset, ut patres egestate laborantes ab op-
pignoratione, si non venditione liberorum, abstinerent: utraque hac
patribus interdixit Constantinus Magnus Lege II. Cod. Theod. de alimentis,
quæ inopes parentes de publico petere debent.

l.i: Imp. Constantinus Augustus Menandro.
Provinciales egestate victus atque alimoniæ inopia laborantes, liberos suos vendere vel
obpignorare cognouimus. Quisquis igitur huiusmodi reperietur, qui nulla rei familiaris
substantia fultus est, quique liberos suos ægre ac difficile sustentet: per fiscum nostrum
antequam fiat calamitati obnoxius, adiuetur[?]: ita ut Proconsules, Præsidesque &
Rationales per universam Africam habeant potestatem, & vniuersis quos aduerterint,
in egestate miserabili constitutos, stipem[?] necessariam largiantur: atque ex horreis
substantiam protinus tribuant competentem. abhorret enim nostris moribus, ut quenquam
fame confici, vel ad indignum facinus prorumpere concedamus. Dat. prid. Non. Iul. Ro-

page.notes: Several doubtful readings are marked [?] in the text: "adiuetur", "stipem" (the long s is read as an f-like stroke), "testatur" (the phrase seems struck through or overprinted, with a doubtful "d" before "Lege X.C."), and "sanguinolentos" in the Constantine rescript, where the line seems to run into "nolentos". The gathering mark "X" below the text is read as a signature. The printed "omnino omnino" is kept as printed. The "Digitized by Google" watermark at the bottom right is left out.
